It’s like he’s melting down. ... “It’s really ESPN. I mean, they run their company the way they want to run their company, but man, it is a shame for the viewer.” It's election day in America, and Morning Joe spent over two minutes discussing the country's most pressing issue: Pat McAfee ruining College GameDay "I don't know if they haven't gotten the message yet, but the manosphere that we all thought was brought in in '24, it may get… pic.twitter.com/a16be985Zt — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 3, 2026 McAfee revealed there have been death threats against him as a result of the controversy surrounding ESPN’s “College GameDay” visit to Utah. “I’ve stayed away from my mentions and DMs this month since these back to back days but ... item.title: The secret behind Miami's explosive offense? A Louisiana country boy who almost walked away from football
item.description: CORAL GABLES, Fla. — The wallpaper of Shannon Dawson's office is a tapestry of a football coach's first language: Xs and Os. Scribbled in black marker, scrawled across three of four walls in the Miami offensive coordinator's digs are play designs, route concepts and offensive formations. You can barely make them out. A film junkie, Dawson's office is often dimly lit as a television glows from across the room. But as the lights flicker on, the walls come alive. There's a surprise here too: a fourth wall — a window looking out to the team's indoor practice facility — is also covered in play designs. Window or wall, no surface can escape Dawson's felted weapon. "We call it 'The Think Tank,'" Dawson says of the window, which, unlike the three walls, holds concepts to be used at a later date instead of the current game week. A country boy at heart, his accent dripping with those south Louisiana and Mississippi roots, the 49-year-old Dawson helps steer the nation's most explosive offense for the country's top-ranked team. Miami deploys college football's most efficient and productive quarterback (Darian Mensah completes 80% of his passes and throws for the sixth-most yards in the sport); its most electrifying receiver (Malachi Toney has caught the second-most touchdowns); and two bruising backs (Mark Fletcher and Javian Mallory combine for 16 scores). As the unbeaten Hurricanes barrel toward perhaps the most anticipated regular game in college football this year — No. 1 Miami vs. No. 11 Notre Dame in South Bend — Dawson's unit is humming at a breakneck pace: no team averages more points a game (46.7); no one has gained more first downs (224); and only one other program gains more yards per snap (7.7). How? The short answer is that coach Mario Cristobal has stockpiled talent; created a hotly competitive team environment; developed athletes into fierce football players; and, four years ago, took a giant leap: He hired Houston's offensive coordinator, then a somewhat unknown disciple of the Air Raid offense who, in his biggest job (Kentucky in 2015) lasted one season. You can find that someone within that dimly lit room, his language sprinkled across wall and window, a man who's blended the pass-heavy concepts of Hal Mumme and Mike Leach with Cristobal's intensely physical running game to produce something altogether scary for opposing defenses. "Adapt or die," Cristobal says from his office on hiring Dawson, perhaps not dissimilar to Nick Saban plucking Lane Kiffin in 2014 to reinvent his offense. "Shannon has been able to morph the principles of the Air Raid with the power running game and screen game. He feels like we're just starting to hit our stride." Keeping the game small Now living near Jackson, Mississippi and, at least for now, out of coaching, Hal Mumme has watched the Hurricanes enough to recognize his system, as well as the country-talk'n Louisiana man who paces the sideline and who he hired in 2003. item.description: Sam Houston girls basketball players, from left, Laniya Lee (No. 11), Jakiyah Caldwell (No. 1), Faira Starks (No. 3) and Sasha Harris (No. 21) pose for a portrait at Sam Houston High School in San Antonio, Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. With experience and chemistry fueled by the return of four returning starters and two other letterwinners, the Hurricanes believe they can buck that trend this season. "Team chemistry is really important, especially since four starters are back," junior forward Laniya Lee said. "We get to build on our chemistry every day during practice, and it shows during the games." Lee returns as does senior guard Jakiah Caldwell and junior guard Faira Starks - "The Big Three" - plus sophomore forward Sasha Harris. Each of them have started since their freshman seasons. That accounts for a lot of varsity minutes playing for coach Chancy Campbell that they hope will pay off this season. "Playing with Coach Chancy, he expects a lot from us," Starks said. "High expectations. Starting as freshmen on varsity, that's really good for us. We're meeting his expectations and they are higher expectations as we get older." The Hurricanes enter 2026-27 as two-time reigning district champions. Sam Houston shared the 27-5A title with Burbank with a 15-1 league mark last season. item.title: Pochettino blends Pulisic, Balogun with youngsters for Haiti clashes
item.description: Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun sustained injuries during the World Cup (Dean Mouhtaropoulos) United States coach Mauricio Pochettino on Wednesday recalled Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun alongside several promising young stars in his squad for the upcoming CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals against Haiti. Neither Pulisic nor Balogun have played for the US since suffering injuries at this summer's World Cup and subsequently missed the start of their club seasons with AC Milan and Monaco respectively. Pulisic fractured his leg during the United States' round-of-16 World Cup loss to Belgium. Striker Balogun -- who was at the heart of a controversy when his ban for a red card during the World Cup was suspended following President Donald Trump's intervention -- sustained a knee injury and was embroiled in a complicated transfer saga. "I think Balo, it's a great opportunity to keep helping him to evolve after a tough summer, after the World Cup," said Pochettino. "Happy to see again Balo because I think after the World Cup, we have the possibility to see, and it is a great opportunity for him to keep improving in his confidence." For the clashes with Haiti on November 14 and 17, the national team mainstays will be joined by a raft of youngsters including Justin Ellis, 19, and Julian Hall, 18. Both made their debuts and scored during the United States' international window in September and October, in which Pochettino's youthful roster won all four games against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. "I think it's a great opportunity for different players now, and for a different roster than was in the last camp, to have the possibility to mix younger with experienced players," said Pochettino. "The combination in between Balogun, Ellis and Hall I think is perfect," he added. Seventeen year-olds Cavan Sullivan and Mathis Albert are also among the attacking options in Pochettino's squad. Meanwhile 21-year-old Santiago Castaneda, a US-Colombian midfielder who plays for German club SC Paderborn, earned his first international senior call-up. The 'away' leg of the quarter-finals will take place in Miami, Florida on November 14, followed by the home leg three days later in Cincinnati, Ohio. The US won the first three CONCACAF Nations League tournaments, between 2021-2024, but suffered an embarrassing semi-final defeat to Panama in last year's edition. item.title: Former offensive stars headline Alabama standouts from NFL Week 8
item.description: Eight weeks are in the books in the NFL, and it was another big weekend for former Alabama Crimson Tide football players at the next level. Two former Alabama players played a big role in one of the biggest games in the NFL this past weekend as the Detroit Lions handed the Minnesota Vikings their first loss as the NFC North race continues to excite. Meanwhile, in a couple of offensive shootouts, two defenders had big days as well. Here is a look at five of Alabama's biggest standouts from Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season. Jahmyr Gibbs, Running Back - Detroit Lions Jahmyr Gibbs continues to look like one of the best running backs in the NFL as he had a big day in helping the Lions give the Vikings their first loss. Gibbs finished with 23 carries for 153 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown. He also added two catches for 15 yards. Gibbs did so against one of the NFL's top defenses. He currently sits second in the NFL in rushing this season. Jameson Williams, Wide Receiver - Detroit Lions Just like Gibbs, Jameson Williams also had a nice day against the Vikings stout defense in helping the Lions to a 19-15 win. Williams finished with four catches for 70 yards and a touchdown. His touchdown was the game-winner that put the Lions ahead with under five minutes remaining. Quinnen Williams, Defensive Tackle - Dallas Cowboys Quinnen Williams has started to catch fire. Even in a 33-30 overtime loss, Williams finished with two sacks amongst seven total tackles. He was one of five players across the league this week to finish with two or more sacks, and he led that group in tackles. Williams has five sacks in the Cowboys last four games. Jordan Battle, Safety - Cincinnati Bengals In a shootout 43-36 win over the Titans, Jordan Battle put up big tackle numbers. He finished the game with twelve tackles, nine of which were solo stops. He also had a pair of pass breakups. JK Scott, Punter - Los Angeles Chargers Not much has gone right this season for the Chargers, and that continued in Week 8 as they fell 24-9 to the Rams. However, JK Scott had arguably his best game of the season which, to be fair, that shows just how much things did not go right. He punted four times for an average of 47.8 yards per punt. He put three of his punts inside the 20 and did not have any touchbacks. His long was 57 yards. item.title: Anthony Richardson Voices Strong Statement on Colts’ QB Situation With Daniel Jones After Week 8
item.description: Anthony Richardson Sr. will continue to serve as chief backup to Daniel Jones . The Indianapolis Colts have made the decision to keep starting Jones, at least for their upcoming Week 9 game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Colts head coach Shane Steichen appeared to be considering making a switch from Jones to Richardson following the team’s brutal 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville. But on Monday, Steichen touched on why Indianapolis’ QB1 role remains in the hands of Jones. “Obviously, the quarterback takes the brunt of it all,” Steichen said, via Stephen Holder of ESPN . “As we know, that’s what the quarterback signs up for. And it’s not all on him, right? It’s everything. It’s all encompassing. It’s everyone doing their job, being on the same page, the route discipline, the route detail, the blocking, the protections — all those things tie into it.” Anthony Richardson Continues to Believe in Jones Nov 1, 2026; Jacksonville, Florida, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. item.title: Mike Vrabel addresses Patriots rumors ahead of NFL trade deadline
item.description: A pair of New England Patriots veterans found themselves in trade rumors ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline . This week, defensive tackle Christian Barmore and cornerback Carlton Davis were mentioned as potential trade candidates by Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer. According to Breer, trading either player would give New England an opportunity to add needed draft capital while getting younger. Speaking on Wednesday, head coach Mike Vrabel responded to the report. “I think sometimes national reports have the tendency to do that. I have not shared that information with anybody,” Vrabel said. “You know, this time of year, I think that all these things kind of get drummed up. So we’re focused on trying to prepare for Green Bay, make the corrections from the game. I mean, this is business as normal here. So, I don’t know where a lot of these things come from. Certainly not any conversations with me.” Davis, 29, has played in four games this season while dealing with a neck injury. When healthy, he has occupied his usual starting role opposite Christian Gonzalez, with Vrabel highlighting his physicality and competitiveness. Barmore, 27, has seen his playing time decrease slightly, playing just 50% of New England’s defensive snaps this season after logging 65% last year. The defensive tackle has been productive at times, recording 3.5 sacks, his highest total since 2023. Neither player has guaranteed money remaining on his contract beyond this season, making a potential trade a realistic possibility. However, would dealing away two defensive contributors make sense for a 5-3 Patriots team with aspirations of competing? “I don’t know. There’s probably a bunch of ways we can make this team better,” Vrabel responded. “You know, coach better, execute better, whether that’s [adding] guys on the streets or — there’s multiple ways. Again, we’d have these conversations each and every day.” Vrabel said he doesn’t feel the need to discuss trade rumors with players, instead keeping conversations centered on football and the team’s preparation. The NFL trade deadline is set for Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. With less than a week to finalize any moves, Vrabel’s focus remains on the present. “Right now, there’ll be another week before the trade deadline,” Vrabel said. “We’ll be leaving for Munich next week. We’re focused on today and how we get better and how we can run the ball better, how we can affect the quarterback. All these things that if we don’t do, it’s going to be tough.”

item.title: Maria Voskamp’s Bold Shot Proves Golf Is A Game Of Guts
item.description: A ball rests near the hole at the OSAA Class 5A State Golf Championships at Emerald Valley Golf & Resort in Creswell Tuesday, May 16, 2023. Most golfers freeze when they see a front pin. They aim for the middle of the green just to stay in play. Maria Voskamp did the exact opposite, and it paid off in a big way. Voskamp stood on the 14th hole at Picton Golf & Country Club with 120 yards to the pin. She had been playing golf for only about a season and a half, but she was ready to take her shot. With an 8-iron in hand, she sent the ball toward the flag. The shot landed roughly five yards to the left of the hole before fading right and dropping straight into the cup. The group behind her started cheering before she even knew what had happened. Voskamp thought her eyes were playing tricks on her until the noise started. It was her first hole-in-one. This moment proves that hesitation can be the real enemy on the course. You cannot win by simply trying to avoid trouble. The math of playing it safe Golf Canada tracks hole-in-one stories every month , and its October 2026 report highlights six different aces. The stories show that golfers of all experience levels can pull off the shot of a lifetime. Kim Koss rang the clubhouse bell at Earl Grey Golf Club after a 163-yard ace with a 6-iron. Kathy Thompson used an 8-iron to ace a 108-yard hole at Stanhope Golf & Country Club. These numbers show that distance matters less than the decision to take the shot. The odds are brutal for an average player, but they are not zero. Voskamp has only played for 1.5 seasons, and she already has her first ace. She picked up the game after six knee surgeries from playing contact sports. Her story is a reminder that you do not need decades of experience to make a memorable shot. Why fear kills your score Many players think playing safe is the smart move. They believe hitting the center of the green saves them from big numbers. That logic can fail when the pin is in a good position. Voskamp’s hole-in-one is a reminder that confidence matters. She took her shot, committed to the swing, and watched the ball find the cup. The report from Golf Canada confirms that these stories are real and that they happen more often than many golfers realize. Voskamp hit it well, and she was pleased that it looked close. She did not know it had gone in until the cheers started. She did not get lucky; she got brave. Stop playing for the middle of the green when the pin is in a good spot. The ball goes where you tell it to go when you commit to the shot. Voskamp struck an 8-iron from 120 yards and watched it settle into the cup. Kim Koss hit a 6-iron from 163 yards and saw her ball disappear into the hole. These are the moments that make golf unforgettable. Sometimes, the best shot is the one you have the guts to take.

item.description: ‘They deserve it’ – Kostas Tsimikas admits familiar failing cost Liverpool in Istanbul Kostas Tsimikas admitted that Liverpool got what they deserved in their 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce in Istanbul on Wednesday. The Reds were in front twice at the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium but still contrived to come away with nothing against Dirk Kuyt’s side, who claimed all three points thanks to Vedat Muriqi’s 79th-minute header. Jeremy Jacquet was criticised for turning his back on Mason Greenwood’s free kick for the first equaliser, and Alisson Becker was culpable of poor positioning for Archie Brown’s goal to make it 2-2. Tsimikas: Fenerbahce deserved to win Speaking to UEFA.com after the match, Tsimikas magnanimously conceded that Fenerbahce were full value for their win and lamented Liverpool’s defending over the goals that they shipped. The Greek defender said (via BBC Sport ): “Congratulations to Fenerbahce, they deserve it. We didn’t play how we had to play. We didn’t defend after the goal we conceded. After three or four minutes, automatically we conceded another goal. “I think we have to mark better if we want to win games. We didn’t play very good and that’s why we lost.” (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust The debrief will be unpleasant for Liverpool It sums up how careless Liverpool were this evening that they were in the lead twice and occupied a winning position for only eight minutes against Fenerbahce, with the goals from Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak cancelled out all too quickly. The manner of all three goals that the home side scored will enrage Iraola – it wasn’t as though the Istanbul outfit had to produce moments of magic to inspire their way to victory over the Reds. Tsimikas himself was far from convincing, enduring a ‘tough night’ in the words of Liverpool Echo reporter Paul Gorst as he struggled to contain the threat of Greenwood, and he ended up being substituted for Milos Kerkez with 15 minutes remaining. Liverpool have now conceded 10 goals in their four Champions League matches, shipping three for the third European fixture in a row, a record which’ll surely concern the head coach at this phase of the competition. The debrief from this game will not be a pleasant one, and a much better defensive performance will be required if the Reds are to return to winning ways against Crystal Palace on Sunday.

item.description: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool saw their UEFA Champions League winning ways come to an end on Wednesday -Credit:Ferda Demir, Getty Images Liverpool led on two occasions but ultimately lost at Fenerbahçe as their flawless UEFA Champions League run ended on a waterlogged evening in Istanbul.
